A routine probe is entered at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:460](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:460), not only after CP failure. The CP keeps the AP pbuf asynchronously after `bmsg_tx_sender()` at [cif_wifi_dp.c:229](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:229) and queues it to hardware at [rwnx_tx.c:715](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:715); it returns ownership only through [cif_mem_mgmt.c:8](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_mem_mgmt.c:8). Reusing the slot at [bk7258_wifi.c:794](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:794) can overwrite a pbuf, frame, or TX descriptor still referenced by CP/DMA.  
**Fix:** do not reclaim or reuse accepted TX slots on `PROBING`, `ABORTING`, or generic mailbox loss. Quarantine them until their `need_free` completion returns, or add an explicit CP Wi-Fi datapath flush/reset handshake that proves the radio queues no longer reference AP memory.

2. **Critical: link-state reset leaves ring indices pointing at stale entries and can resend stale CP pointers.**  
[bk7258_wifi.c:705](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:705) clears only `node_count`, `recycle_count`, and `packet_count`; none of the corresponding head/tail indices are reset. If `head != tail`, the next enqueue writes at the old tail while the next dequeue reads the old head. For the recycle ring, [bk7258_wifi.c:526](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:526) can therefore send an old CPDU address after CP has reused that memory. Concurrent `wifi_receive()` can also decrement a count reset to zero at [bk7258_wifi.c:863](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:863), underflowing it to 255.  
**Fix:** serialize link reset with all ring producers/consumers, reset every head, tail, and count together, and invalidate queued entries by recovery generation. Perform the reset in the Wi-Fi worker or under one shared lock, not asynchronously in the diagnostic callback.

3. **High: the AP rejects valid CP data lists larger than eight, leaking CP pbufs under traffic.**  
The AP hard-limits lists to eight at [bk7258_wifi_ipc.h:29](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_wifi_ipc.h:29) and rejects larger lists at [bk7258_wifi.c:552](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:552). The CP supports 60 RX buffers at [cif_main.h:67](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_main.h:67) and sends the entire pending `co_list_cnt()` in one node at [cif_main.c:253](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_main.c:253). On rejection, CP's completion callback ignores ACK failure and merely clears `sending_flag` at [cif_main.c:277](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_main.c:277), while the list was already cleared at [cif_main.c:269](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_main.c:269). Those pbufs are never recycled.  
**Fix:** either support at least `MAX_NUM_RX_BUFFERS` entries on AP, with bounded cycle/range validation, or batch CP lists to eight and retain each unsent/failed suffix until a successful ACK.

4. **High: recycle-queue overflow leaves CP pbuf ownership metadata permanently corrupted.**  
`wifi_recycle_append()` increments `pbuf->ref`, sets `need_free`, and rewires `next` at [bk7258_wifi.c:469](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:469) before ensuring a recycle queue slot exists. If the queue is full, [bk7258_wifi.c:651](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:651) drops the constructed list and only lowers carrier. CP expects the extra reference and return message before performing the paired decrement/free at [cif_wifi_dp.c:169](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:169). The result is leaked pbufs and a modified list that neither side owns safely.  
**Fix:** reserve a recycle queue entry before modifying any CP memory, then commit the node atomically. If reservation or sending fails, retain the fully constructed node for retry; never discard it after changing `ref`, `flags`, or `next`.

5. **High: Wi-Fi backpressure is converted into a terminal mailbox ACK, losing transferred ownership.**  
When the Wi-Fi node queue is full, [bk7258_wifi.c:673](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:673) returns `-EAGAIN`. The mailbox layer treats every callback error as `COM_FAIL` at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:688](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:688) and sends an ACK, so the physical descriptor is not deferred. CP completion code does not inspect the failure and has already detached the list, producing leaked RX pbufs, stuck AP TX slots, or exhausted event buffers.  
**Fix:** give `-EAGAIN` true retry semantics: release the uncommitted ACK slot, retain the received command descriptor, and retry it when the Wi-Fi worker signals capacity. Only send an ACK after the Wi-Fi layer has durably accepted ownership.

6. **Medium: a confirmation racing the command timeout poisons the next command semaphore wait.**  
After `nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible()` times out at [bk7258_wifi.c:215](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:215), `waiting_id` remains armed until [bk7258_wifi.c:229](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:229). The next command never drains/resets `command_sem`, so it can wake immediately with its freshly initialized `-ETIMEDOUT`, causing commands to remain one response behind.  
**Fix:** protect arm/disarm and event matching with one synchronization primitive, reset/drain the semaphore before arming each sequence, and atomically disarm plus drain after timeout. A per-command generation/result state is preferable to relying on semaphore count alone.
